cells.tense: This is happening now and you're the one looking, holding more open than most people can sit with.
cells.ask: Let what you see turn into one concrete step, say the version out loud, and let that fix it.
cells.core:
You can hold more open than most people can sit with. Something like a read on a whole situation arrives before any of the parts have names, and you don't rush it into a decision to feel better. That's a real gift, and it's doing work right now.

The balance runs one way: what you see stays clean as long as it's feeding thinking you actually use. When it starts feeding itself — more angles, more openness, the pleasure of not-yet — the depth stops coming back out as anything you'd act on. The ask is to give one thing a shape and let the shape cost you the other options. Then the next thing you see has somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole thing before it has parts. Give one of them a shape.
cells.verb: seeing before there's anything in particular to see
cells.place: standing in what hasn't taken shape yet

cells.tense: What's coming hasn't arrived yet and you're already bracing for how it might go.
cells.ask: Stand in the plainest thing in front of you, noticing only what's actually there, for a full minute without deciding anything.
cells.core:
There's a version out ahead where everything is clear, and you've moved into it — running the possibilities faster than the situation is moving. It looks like foresight. It's tension.

Real seeing doesn't push. It arrives when there's nothing to make it prove itself. At the moment the next thing has to meet a standard before you'll stand in it — you're holding up what's in front of you by testing it against a future that hasn't happened. Drop your shoulders and let the thing in front of you be nothing more than what it is. The freshness you're scanning for is in this second, and it won't come while you're bracing.
cells.sheetLine: You're scanning for what's next instead of seeing what's here.

cells.tense: Something got decided back there and you're still standing at the door as if it hadn't.
cells.ask: Name one clear thing you saw and take one step this week that only makes sense if it's true.
cells.core:
When this is working, you look at a situation and one reading stands out without effort. You trust it enough to say what you see. Latest situations are getting the held-breath treatment instead. You stay available to everything, and committing to one reading feels like too much. What you see goes quiet and doesn't come back out as anything you move on.

The sight itself hasn't gone anywhere. What's short is the willingness to let it have consequences. Pick one read still alive in you, do the next real thing it points to. The point isn't whether you're right. Following through keeps the next clear look possible.
cells.sheetLine: You saw something real and didn't act on it. Start with one.

cells.tense: Right now your looking is shaping where this goes, and you're treating it as something that just happens to you.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you saw this week that turned out true, and say out loud that you saw it.
cells.core:
You see more than you take credit for. The read you have on people and situations is yours — you make it, it doesn't descend on you — but you talk about what you notice as if it simply arrived. 'The situation is like this,' not 'I see it like this.' So what you see keeps working without the claim.

Nothing needs fixing in how you see. What's missing is the ownership. Someone disagrees with your read and it lands as a question about you, because you haven't said the read was yours to begin with. Say it as yours. You can hold it and still let someone else be right, and each time you admit you're the one who saw it, the next clear look arrives easier.
cells.sheetLine: You're seeing it. You haven't said the seeing is yours.
